title: As He is, be (Mekhilta, Shirata 3)
hookLine: as God is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful
tomorrow: how do you follow someone who is a fire?

lines: THE SONG ON THE FAR SHORE.
cards: Everybody copies someone. An older cousin's laugh, a coach's handshake, the way a favorite singer signs her name. Now back to the shore.
The water has closed behind them. Moses and the people are singing, and in the middle of the song comes a line the old Jewish translation gives as "This is my God, and I will glorify Him."
Much later, in the Mekhilta, a book of midrash on Exodus, the sages stop on that last word. Glorify God? With what?
A person can't add one thing to God. So what is the line asking for?

teach.b: The Hebrew word is ve'anvehu, and the Mekhilta gives more than one answer. Rabbi Ishmael says: make your mitzvot beautiful before God. A lovely sukkah, a lovely prayer shawl.
Then a sage named Abba Shaul hears something hiding inside the word.
Say it slowly and it echoes ani ve-hu: I and He. So he reads the verse as a job description. Be like Him.
As He is gracious and merciful, so you be gracious and merciful. Look at what he picks. Not the power that split the sea.

teach.h: COPY THE MERCY, NOT THE POWER.
teach.b: Of everything the song just praised, the part a person is asked to copy is mercy, two words from the list God gives Moses about Himself later in Exodus.

Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: the rabbis turned a sound inside a word into a way of life, and the way of life is kindness. The Talmud brings Abba Shaul's reading again, in tractate Shabbat.
And it quietly changes what imitating God means. Nobody becomes God.
You copy the one thing a person actually can: going easy on someone who can't pay you back.
Yesterday a servant girl saw God at the sea. Abba Shaul asks what you do once you've seen.

how: Jewish teaching often names imitating God's kindness as a duty: Abba Shaul's reading in the Mekhilta, and again in the Talmud (Shabbat 133b), is taught as 'be like Him: as He is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful.'

o: sing God's praise aloud, the way the people did
be gracious and merciful, the way God is
be strong and just, the way God is at the sea

games.q: one word, two readings — tap the pairs.
p: hears 'I and He' inside one word
this is my God, and I will glorify Him
the part of God a person can copy

s: imitating God means copying God's power
Abba Shaul picks mercy: as He is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful.
Abba Shaul's reading starts from the sound of one Hebrew word
ve'anvehu, heard as ani ve-hu: I and He.
the Mekhilta gives only one reading of the verse
Rabbi Ishmael reads the same word as making your mitzvot beautiful.

games.q: a coworker botched an order and the customer is yelling at her. you saw the mistake coming. by Abba Shaul's reading, what comes first?
o: make it clear the mistake was hers, so the record is fair.
step in and help her fix it, and never mention you saw it coming.
stay out of it; being merciful means not getting involved.
games.why: as He is gracious and merciful, so be. mercy here is an act: going easy on someone who can't pay you back, not just staying neutral.

practice: Bring to mind one person who will need some grace from you this week: a little brother, a coworker running late, someone about to get something wrong in front of you. Picture the moment it happens.
Now choose, ahead of time, one gracious thing you'll say or do, small enough that you'll really do it, and keep that plan in front of you while the bell rings out.

wordCard.voice: As He is: Abba Shaul's reading of one word in the song at the sea. As God is gracious and merciful, so be gracious and merciful.

orig.note: Hebrew: and I will glorify Him (Exodus 15:2). Abba Shaul hears ani ve-hu, I and He, inside it.

carryVoice: Your line: as he is, be. Of everything at the sea, mercy is the part a person can copy.

sources.ref: Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael, Beshallach, Shirata 3 (on Exodus 15:2: Rabbi Ishmael on beautifying the mitzvot; Abba Shaul: be like Him, as He is gracious and merciful)
